TO: Engagement Team — Funds & Asset Management Practice
FROM: Investment Advisory Group
RE: Redline Review of Counterparty Markup of Investment Advisory Agreement

This memorandum provides a comprehensive redline review of the counterparty's markup of the Investment Advisory Agreement (the "Agreement") against our firm's standard form investment advisory agreement (the "Standard Form") and the internal funds asset management negotiation playbook (the "Playbook"). The counterparty has returned a marked-up version of the Agreement (the "Redline") containing a series of proposed deviations. This analysis identifies each material deviation, assesses it against firm precedent and prevailing market practice in the funds asset management industry, and recommends an accept / reject / counter position.

The deliverable is structured as follows: (I) Purpose and Scope; (II) Summary of Standard Form and Playbook Framework; (III) Material Deviations and Recommended Positions; (IV) Non-Material / Administrative Changes; (V) Outstanding Open Items and Conditions to Closing; and (VI) Conclusion and Recommended Strategy.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
II. SUMMARY OF STANDARD FORM AND PLAYBOOK FRAMEWORK
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A. Standard Form Architecture

Our Standard Form investment advisory agreement is organized around the following core pillars, each of which corresponds to a defined scope of legal and commercial risk allocation:

1. Representations and Warranties. Mutual representations covering authority, enforceability, and no-conflict; investment adviser registration status under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 and applicable state laws; accuracy of disclosure documents; and absence of litigation or regulatory proceedings materially affecting performance of the Agreement.

2. Scope of Advisory Services and Authority. Definition of the discretionary / non-discretionary authority granted to the adviser, including investment guidelines, custody arrangements, and delegated voting authority.

3. Fees and Compensation. Fee schedule, calculation methodology, invoicing and payment timing, and fee disclosure obligations.

4. Covenants. Ongoing covenants regarding compliance with applicable law, books and records, regulatory filings, maintenance of registration, and prompt notice of material events.

5. Conditions to Closing / Effectiveness. Conditions precedent to the effective date, including delivery of executed documents, registration in good standing, and absence of material adverse change.

6. Indemnification. Reciprocal (mutual) indemnification for breaches of representations, gross negligence, willful misconduct, and violations of law, with cap and survival structure.

7. Termination. Termination for convenience (with notice), for cause, for change of control, and automatic termination upon the adviser's loss of registration.

8. Miscellaneous. Governing law, assignment, notices, entire agreement, severability, no third-party beneficiaries, and dispute resolution.

B. Internal Playbook Positions

The Playbook establishes the following baseline negotiating posture for a funds asset management engagement:

* Maintain mutual, balanced indemnification. Resist shifting to one-sided adviser indemnification for client performance risk outside the adviser's control.

* Preserve the adviser's discretion. Avoid language converting discretionary advisory authority into a guarantee of performance or a fiduciary performance standard that is inconsistent with market norms.

* Guard the cap and survival structure. Fee-related indemnities typically carry no cap; other breach indemnities carry a negotiated cap tied to fees or a fixed multiple. Survival periods should align with industry norms (typically two (2) years for representations, with longer periods for fundamental representations).

* Scope termination for cause to material breach with a reasonable cure period. Reject termination on mere convenience without adequate notice, and reject for-cause triggers that are vague or overbroad.

* Condition effectiveness on regulatory good standing. The adviser's registration and compliance posture must remain a gate to closing.

* Reject non-standard regulatory indemnities. Do not accept indemnification for client-directed investment decisions or indemnification triggered by changes in law that are not the adviser's fault.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
III. MATERIAL DEVIATIONS AND RECOMMENDED POSITIONS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Redline introduces a number of material departures from the Standard Form and Playbook. Each material deviation is catalogued below with our recommendation.

A. Representations and Warranties

Deviation 1 - Expanded Adviser Representation Regarding Past Performance Track Record. The Redline adds a new representation obligating the adviser to represent that all historical performance data, track records, and marketing materials are accurate and not materially misleading, with the representation extending to "all statements made by the adviser or any of its controlled affiliates in any presentation."

Assessment: This materially broadens the adviser's exposure beyond the client's account to encompass all marketing and promotional materials, including materials prepared for other clients and prospective investors. It is not market standard and substantially exceeds typical performance-data representations, which are generally limited to data provided in connection with the specific account.

Recommendation: REJECT AS DRAFTED; COUNTER. Narrow the representation to historical performance data and track records specifically provided to the client in connection with the engagement. Strike the extension to "controlled affiliates" and "all statements made ... in any presentation." Redline to limit to information "reasonably relied upon by the Client in deciding to retain the Adviser."

Deviation 2 - Deletion of Mutual No-Conflict Representation. The Redline deletes the mutual "no conflict" representation from the client.

Assessment: The Standard Form includes a mutual no-conflict representation covering both parties. Deleting the client-side counterpart narrows the adviser's protections and is inconsistent with the mutual-representation framework in the Playbook.

Recommendation: REJECT; RESTORE. Restore the mutual no-conflict representation on the client side.

B. Scope of Advisory Services and Authority

Deviation 3 - Conversion of Discretionary Authority to a Performance Standard. The Redline revises the description of the adviser's authority to state that the adviser shall exercise its discretion "in a manner designed to achieve the Client's target return and risk parameters as set forth in Exhibit A."

Assessment: This language risks being construed as a guarantee of target returns or an elevated fiduciary standard qualitatively different from professional investment discretion. It converts the adviser's best-efforts discretionary mandate into a quantity-of-performance benchmark, creating significant and inappropriate liability.

Recommendation: REJECT; COUNTER. Restore the Standard Form "full and complete discretion ... consistent with the investment guidelines and applicable law." Remove any reference to "achieving" target returns or defined outcomes. If the client seeks a reference to objectives, use permissive language reflecting that the guidelines "reflect the Client's objectives" without imposing an outcome obligation.

Deviation 4 - Proposed Sub-Adviser / Delegation Restriction. The Redline inserts an unqualified restriction barring the adviser from delegating any discretionary duties to sub-advisers without the client's prior written consent in each instance.

Assessment: Standard practice permits the adviser to engage and replace sub-advisers for client accounts subject to notice requirements and, where required by the advisory agreement, consent. An unqualified per-instance consent requirement removes operational flexibility and is not market standard.

Recommendation: REJECT; COUNTER. Adopt a framework permitting delegation to sub-advisers with prior written notice, with consent required only where the fund platform or client mandate explicitly requires it, and confirm that the adviser retains responsibility for sub-adviser acts.

C. Fees and Compensation

Deviation 5 - Fee Audit / Look-Back Right. The Redline adds a client right to audit the adviser's fee calculations, including a look-back to records for the prior three (3) fiscal years, with the adviser bearing the cost of any audit that reveals an error exceeding a de minimis threshold.

Assessment: A fee audit right is reasonably market standard, but a three-year look-back coupled with adviser-paid audit costs and a low de minimis threshold is aggressive.

Recommendation: ACCEPT IN PART; COUNTER. Accept the audit right with reasonable confidentiality protections and advance notice. Limit the look-back to records maintained for the current and prior fiscal year, consistent with books-and-records retention, and raise the de minimis threshold to a materiality threshold (e.g., 0.5% of aggregate fees charged for the audited period) before the adviser bears audit costs.

D. Covenants

Deviation 6 - Expanded Compliance Covenant. The Redline adds a covenant requiring the adviser to "maintain a compliance program reasonably designed to prevent violations of the Advisers Act" and to deliver, upon request, its compliance policies, adoption-required compliance reports, and its annual compliance review summary.

Assessment: The adviser must already maintain a compliance program under Rule 206(4)-7 of the Advisers Act. The concern is the mandated production of the annual compliance review summary and internal policies, which are confidential and not the subject of a customary client information right.

Recommendation: ACCEPT the affirmance of the compliance program obligation in substance (which mirrors existing regulatory duty) but COUNTER the documentary production requirement. Restrict production to the annual Form ADV Part 2A brochure and updates, and permit review of policies only in connection with a regulatory audit, under confidentiality, not as a general client entitlement.

Deviation 7 - New Covenant to Deliver Side Letter / Fee Breakpoints to Other Clients. The Redline adds a most-favored-nation (MFN) style covenant entitling the client to the benefit of any more favorable fee arrangement the adviser later offers to "similarly situated" accounts.

Assessment: An MFN fee covenant is uncommon in institutional investment advisory agreements and creates ongoing administrative and interpretive burden.

Recommendation: REJECT. Advise the client that the mutual fee schedule is set in Exhibit A and that an MFN covenant is not standard. If the client insists, counter to restrict MFN to identical strategy and asset-size accounts, require the fee break to be self-effectuating through written notice only, and delete any retroactive recomputation.

E. Conditions to Closing / Effectiveness

Deviation 8 - Additional Conditions Precedent. The Redline adds conditions to the effective date requiring (i) the adviser to deliver a "compliance certification" signed by the Chief Compliance Officer and (ii) no "material adverse change" in the adviser's managed assets or ratings.

Assessment: The compliance certification is redundant with the adviser's statutory obligations and registration status already captured in the Standard Form conditions. The "material adverse change" condition referencing managed assets or ratings is vague, extends to events beyond the control of the adviser, and is an unusual gate for agreement effectiveness.

Recommendation: REJECT the MAC condition, which is overbroad and not tied to the adviser's ability to perform. ACCEPT a delimited compliance certification condition substantially limited to confirming the adviser maintains its registration and is not subject to a pending SEC or state proceeding that would prohibit performance.

F. Indemnification

Deviation 9 - Asymmetry Favoring Client. The Redline rewrites the indemnification section to require the adviser to indemnify the client for "any loss, liability, damage or expense ... arising out of or relating to this Agreement or the provision of advisory services," while limiting the client's reciprocal indemnity to the client's "gross negligence or willful misconduct."

Assessment: This is a material and one-sided departure. It converts mutual indemnification into a broad adviser-conduct indemnity with only a narrow reciprocal right for the adviser. The qualifier "relating to the provision of advisory services" is extremely broad and would capture ordinary-course losses not caused by the adviser's breach.

Recommendation: REJECT; RESTORE MUTUAL STRUCTURE. Restore the reciprocal indemnification from the Standard Form, under which each party indemnifies the other for losses arising from that party's breach of representations, gross negligence, willful misconduct, or violation of applicable law. If the client will not accept the full mutual structure, counter with an indemnity limited to the adviser's breach of representations, gross negligence, willful misconduct, and violation of law (mirroring the reciprocal language, dropping the overbroad "arising out of or relating to" scope).

Deviation 10 - Expansion of Covered Losses and Consequential Damages. The Redline deletes the standard limitation excluding indirect, special, consequential, punitive and incidental damages for both parties.

Assessment: Deleting the mutual consequential-damages waiver is a significant redline that materially increases exposure. It is firmly against market practice for both parties to bear unlimited consequential-damage exposure in an advisory agreement.

Recommendation: REJECT; RESTORE. Reinsert the mutual exclusion of indirect, special, consequential, punitive and incidental damages, applied symmetrically to both parties.

Deviation 11 - Removal of Indemnity Cap. The Redline deletes the cap on the adviser's indemnification obligations for non-fee claims.

Assessment: The Standard Form caps non-fee breach indemnities at a negotiated multiple of fees. Deleting the cap leaves the adviser exposed to uncapped liability for ordinary breaches, which is not market standard.

Recommendation: REJECT; RESTORE CAP. Reinsert the negotiated cap for non-fee indemnities (fees-only claims may remain uncapped). If the client objects, counter with a cap in the alternative at a higher multiple, but do not accept an uncapped non-fee indemnity.

G. Termination

Deviation 12 - Termination for Convenience Without Notice. The Redline permits either party to terminate the Agreement for convenience on ten (10) business days' notice, with no transition period.

Assessment: Industry standard for advisory agreements requires reasonable advance notice for convenience termination (typically 60-90 days) to permit orderly transition and wind-down of the account. Ten business days' notice is insufficient.

Recommendation: REJECT; COUNTER. Extend the convenience-termination notice period to sixty (60) days (or, at a minimum, thirty (30) days) to permit orderly transition.

Deviation 13 - Expanded For-Cause Termination. The Redline adds "any breach of this Agreement by the Adviser" as an event of termination-for-cause with no materiality qualifier and no cure period.

Assessment: "Any breach" with no materiality or cure period is overbroad and would permit termination on trivial or inadvertent non-material failures, undermining the mutual-cure architecture of the Standard Form.

Recommendation: REJECT; COUNTER. Restrict termination for cause to a "material breach" that remains uncured for thirty (30) days after written notice, and align cure rights for both parties.

Deviation 14 - Termination on Loss of Registration. The Redline revises the automatic-termination provision to allow the client to terminate only if the adviser "loses registration and fails to re-establish registration within ten (10) days," with no suspension-of-services backstop.

Assessment: Loss of the adviser's registration is a fundamental event that must protect the client while the adviser cures. Ten days is too short to permit the adviser to address regulatory issues, and the provision lacks a mechanism for the adviser to suspend services pending cure.

Recommendation: COUNTER. Provide that loss of registration entitles the client to terminate with a reasonable cure period (e.g., thirty (30) days), during which the adviser may not provide new discretionary services without client consent.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IV. NON-MATERIAL / ADMINISTRATIVE CHANGES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Redline also includes a series of administrative and conforming changes that are acceptable as drafted, subject only to technical confirmation:

* Updated client block / definitions consistent with the current entity names.
* Conforming cross-references to the amended termination and indemnity sections.
* Minor stylistic edits to the notice provision, preserving the existing notice addresses.
* Reformatting of exhibit references.

These changes carry no independent legal or commercial risk and may be accepted, provided they do not interact adversely with the material positions recommended above.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
V. OUTSTANDING OPEN ITEMS AND CONDITIONS TO CLOSING
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The following open items should be resolved before the Agreement is executed:

1. Confirm the effective-date conditions recommended in Section III.E (Deviation 8), so the Agreement's effectiveness is conditioned on the adviser's regulatory good standing rather than an overbroad MAC.

2. Align the final indemnification and cap structure (Deviations 9-11) with the mutual framework before circulation of the execution set.

3. Confirm the termination-for-convenience notice period and the for-cause material breach/cure structure (Deviations 12-13) are incorporated into the final draft.

4. Confirm the CCO/regulatory disclosure posture regarding the newly proposed compliance documentary covenant (Deviation 6) before accepting any production obligation.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
VI. CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDED STRATEGY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The counterparty's markup introduces a materially more one-sided allocation of risk than the Standard Form or the internal Playbook contemplates. Of the material deviations identified, we recommend accepting none in unqualified form. We recommend a strategy of strategic counteroffers across the five thematic areas - representations, scope of authority, fees, indemnification, and termination - designed to return the Agreement to a balanced, market-standard posture while preserving the client relationship.

In summary:

* ACCEPT IN MODIFIED FORM: Fee-audit right (Deviation 5) and the affirmance of a compliance program (Deviation 6), each with the narrowing modifications set out above.
* REJECT / RESTORE: Mutual no-conflict representation (Deviation 2); mutual indemnification and consequential-damages waiver (Deviations 9 and 10); and the indemnity cap (Deviation 11).
* REJECT / COUNTER: Performance-standard discretion language (Deviation 3); sub-adviser consent restriction (Deviation 4); MFN fee covenant (Deviation 7); MAC condition (Deviation 8); convenience and for-cause termination provisions (Deviations 12 and 13); and loss-of-registration cure period (Deviation 14).
* NARROW / COUNTER: Expanded performance-data representation (Deviation 1) and compliance documentary production (Deviation 6).

By advancing these positions, we can bring the Agreement back into line with the Standard Form and internal Playbook while preserving the commercial relationship. Counsel should proceed to issue the responsive markup and negotiate toward a balanced, market-standard final agreement.

management industry, and recommends an accept / reject / counter position.

Standard Form and Playbook Framework; (III) Material Deviations and Recommended
Positions; (IV) Non-Material / Administrative Changes; (V) Outstanding Open Items
and Conditions to Closing; and (VI) Conclusion and Recommended Strategy.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

core pillars, each of which corresponds to a defined scope of legal and commercial
risk allocation:

1. Representations and Warranties. Mutual representations covering authority,
   enforceability, and no-conflict; investment adviser registration status under
   the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 and applicable state laws; accuracy of
   disclosure documents; and absence of litigation or regulatory proceedings
   materially affecting performance of the Agreement.

2. Scope of Advisory Services and Authority. Definition of the discretionary /
   non-discretionary authority granted to the adviser, including investment
   guidelines, custody arrangements, and delegated voting authority.

3. Fees and Compensation. Fee schedule, calculation methodology, invoicing and
   payment timing, and fee disclosure obligations.

4. Covenants. Ongoing covenants regarding compliance with applicable law, books
   and records, regulatory filings, maintenance of registration, and prompt notice
   of material events.

5. Conditions to Closing / Effectiveness. Conditions precedent to the effective
   date, including delivery of executed documents, registration in good standing,
   and absence of material adverse change.

6. Indemnification. Reciprocal (mutual) indemnification for breaches of
   representations, gross negligence, willful misconduct, and violations of law,
   with cap and survival structure.

7. Termination. Termination for convenience (with notice), for cause, for change
   of control, and automatic termination upon the adviser's loss of registration.

8. Miscellaneous. Governing law, assignment, notices, entire agreement,
   severability, no third-party beneficiaries, and dispute resolution.

B. Internal Playbook Positions

The Playbook establishes the following baseline negotiating posture for a funds
asset management engagement:

* Maintain mutual, balanced indemnification. Resist shifting to one-sided adviser
  indemnification for client performance risk outside the adviser's control.

* Preserve the adviser's discretion. Avoid language converting discretionary
  advisory authority into a guarantee of performance or a fiduciary performance
  standard that is inconsistent with market norms.

  cap; other breach indemnities carry a negotiated cap tied to fees or a fixed
  multiple. Survival periods should align with industry norms (typically two (2)
  years for representations, with longer periods for fundamental representations).

* Condition effectiveness on regulatory good standing.

* Reject non-standard regulatory indemnities.

and track records specifically provided to the client in connection with the
engagement.

the mutual "no conflict" representation from the client.

Recommendation: REJECT; RESTORE.

Deviation 3 — Conversion of Discretionary Authority to a Performance Standard.
Recommend REJECT; COUNTER, restoring the Standard Form discretion language.

Deviation 4 — Proposed Sub-Adviser / Delegation Restriction. Recommend REJECT;

Deviation 5 — Fee Audit / Look-Back Right. Recommend ACCEPT IN PART; COUNTER to
limit look-back period and raise materiality threshold.

Deviation 6 — Expanded Compliance Covenant. Recommend ACCEPT in substance;
COUNTER the documentary production requirement.

Deviation 7 — New MFN Fee Covenant. Recommend REJECT.

Deviation 8 — Additional Conditions Precedent. Recommend REJECT the MAC condition;

F. Indemnification

STRUCTURE.

Deviation 10 — Expansion of Covered Losses and Consequential Damages. Recommend

Deviation 11 — Removal of Indemnity Cap. Recommend REJECT; RESTORE CAP.

material breach with cure period.

reasonable cure period.
